text:
alyssa: Heads-up — saw a reconnect spike for a handful of tenants around 09:14 UTC. Console shows a flurry of short-lived SSE sessions and a weird lease jitter pattern.

matt: Which tenants? any common routing policy / region?

alyssa: eu-west-1 primarily, but the pattern looks like: edge sends Keep-Alive TTL 120 -> origin accepts 60 -> client reconnects after ~65s, gets a new lease id. Clusters of quick reconnects for same user id.

jordan: Ugh, did the edge recently change its default keepalive? I pushed the sticky-lease fallback last week but didn't touch ttl.

sam: console graphs look odd too — the session-count timeseries lumps them under a single alias key so it looks like sustained connections, not churn. I think console is stripping the tenant suffix somewhere.

tanya: Can you paste the raw headers from a sample connection (obf keys ok)?

alyssa: sure — snippet:

```
GET /sse/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: inference.redwood.example
X-Tenant: acme-42
X-Session-Lease: lease-7f3b
Keep-Alive: timeout=120
X-Edge-TTL: 120
```

matt: And origin responded with?

alyssa: origin ->

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Session-Lease: lease-7f3b
Keep-Alive: timeout=60
```

sam: So origin is clamping TTL to 60. Edge thinks it's 120, schedules a reconnect later, but client sees session drop earlier (origin closed or GCed). That mismatch -> duplicate leases.

jordan: Where's the authoritative TTL supposed to come from? should edge always defer to origin header or our routing policy config?

tanya: Our design doc says origin is authoritative for lease TTL but the edge should echo the negotiated TTL to the client. If edge used the advertised 120, it should have used the origin's 60 after handshake.

alyssa: Looks like the handshake path didn't pass the origin TTL back to the client for a subset of proxy paths (the new fast-path we flipped last month). Repro: curl -H 'X-Tenant: acme-42' -v

infra-bot: deploy-notice: fast-path-proxy (edge-pool-7) rolled out at 2025-11-02T08:23:00Z

matt: That rollout time lines up. fast-path is probably skipping the TTL echo. On the console side: what's causing the aliasing?

sam: Console summary pipeline removes tenant suffixes for display normalization — but when leases flip quickly we get repeated lease IDs mapped to a single canonical key because the UI grouping only looks at X-Tenant base. The grouping logic ignores X-Session-Lease.

jordan: So two separate problems: (1) edge/origin TTL negotiation bug in fast-path, (2) console grouping hides rapid churn and misleads SREs about sustained sessions.

tanya: Proposed short-term mitigation: roll back fast-path on eu-west-1 and also adjust console sampling to break out session-leases for the next 24h.

alyssa: Agreed. Can someone own rollback and open a console patch? I can take the fast-path rollback if matt can coordinate the canary unroll.

matt: I'll run the rollback canary and watch the session churn. Jordan, can you open a console patch to surface lease IDs in the L4 view? Make it gated behind a flag.

jordan: On it. Patch will add `sessionLease` as visible grouping key and a flag `ui.showLeaseIds`.

sam: Also adding a short-lived alert: "lease-jitter-rate > 5%" so we can catch regressions post-rollback.

infra-bot: playbook: rollback command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/edge-fast-path --namespace=edge --to-revision=1` (run canary on pool-3 first)

matt: Running canary on pool-3 now.

alyssa: Can you post a small postmortem note in incidents/ after we confirm? Want to capture TL;DR and root cause mapping to fast-path handshake.

tanya: I'll prepare the console patch draft and link it here when ready. :thumbsup:

matt: Canary looks good so far — no new reconnects in pool-3. Proceeding with rollback for eu-west-1 on pool-7.

alyssa: Thanks. Once rollback is live, we'll confirm session stability and then follow up with a retro and a test that asserts edge echoes origin TTL when present.

sam: +1 on a unit/integration test for TTL handshake and a small e2e that validates console grouping for rapid lease churn.

infra-bot: alert-created: lease-jitter-rate (eu-west-1) threshold 5% — owners: eng-platform, eng-sre

alyssa: Filing incident doc now. Thanks all.
